# Recurring scheduling and sweeps

The repo-inactivity gate and `run_when_inactive` are in the leaf
[coga/recurring/scheduling/inactivity](inactivity/SKILL.md).

## Periods and the serviced-period ledger

The scan takes each template's last firing strictly before now and buckets it
into a period key: hourly → `YYYY-MM-DD-HH`, daily → `YYYY-MM-DD`, weekly
(day-of-week set) → `YYYY-Www`, monthly (day-of-month set) → `YYYY-MM`,
anything else → `YYYYMMDDTHHMM`.

The high-water mark is a `created|reused <task-ref> for <period>` line tagged
`recurring/<name>` in the repo-global `coga/log.md`. It is not in the template
blackboard, where a run rewriting a region could erase it and re-fire the
period. The greatest valid period evidence survives retention after a period task
is reaped and is never composed into prompts. A period at or below the newest valid record is not
re-created or re-launched. A malformed record is a template error in the
sweep, `coga recurring list` and `coga status`, never "ran this period".

Current period only: missed periods are not chased, so a monthly run of a
weekly template produces one run. A new template's first sweep services the
most recent past firing ([templates](../templates/SKILL.md#first-firing-is-retroactive)).

## Repo scope and clone scope

A template is `scope: repo` (the default) or `scope: clone`. Repo scope is one
shared period task per firing, serviced by whichever clone sweeps first and
recorded in the ledger above. That is right for shared state and wrong for
clone- or machine-local state, which no other clone can see.

A `scope: clone` template is serviced once per period **in every clone that
sweeps**. It requires a reserved `ticket.py` and rejects `delegate`,
`state_keys` and `workflow`. The sweep runs the script directly, after the
shared launches. No period task is created, the runner commits nothing, and no
log line is written; a script's own state changes and publication belong to
its template. The script gets the template's `secrets` and
`COGA_RECURRING_SCOPE=clone`, `COGA_RECURRING_TEMPLATE` and
`COGA_RECURRING_PERIOD`, but no `COGA_TASK_*` variables, so there is nothing to
bump. Exit 0 records the period in `<primary checkout's coga
dir>/.coga/recurring-clone/<name>.json`, with the output beside it in
`<name>.log`; a run from a temporary control worktree counts for the clone that
owns it. Any other exit is a sweep failure, recorded for autofix and retried by
the next sweep. The owner, control-branch and inactivity gates apply as for
repo scope. `--force` and `coga recurring launch <name>` ignore the clone
ledger. `coga recurring list` shows only this clone's state.

Clone scripts have bounded runtime and output. A timeout reports the failure,
terminates the script's process tree and leaves the period retryable, so later
templates still run. Truncated console output points to the local log for the
fi…790 tokens truncated…. A `canceled`
  period gets a controlled refusal; the sweep continues and exits non-zero.
  Force does not bypass branch, owner or TTY gates.
- `coga recurring launch <name>` (and default aliases such as `coga dream`)
  creates or reuses one template's task ignoring schedule and dedup (an explicit
  override when the period's task was reaped); a live run is resumed, a
  prior-period `done` replaced, a non-human `paused` run resumed exactly as a
  sweep would (an agent-backed one refuses without a TTY), and a
  current-period `done` or a human-`paused` run left alone. It passes the sweep's
  concrete idle/max-session limits unless `--interactive`.
- `coga recurring launch <name> --rerun` also replaces a current-period `done`
  task with a fresh run at step 1 from the current template. Each invocation is
  a real run, with the ordinary notifications and state publication. The
  default `coga autoclose` alias includes `--rerun`, so manual cleanup can run
  repeatedly within a day or week. Other aliases and scheduled sweeps keep
  their existing deduplication. Live runs resume; human-paused, blocked and
  canceled runs stay parked. Branch, owner, TTY and concurrent-generation
  checks still apply, as do the cleanup proofs.
- `--interactive` needs an attended TTY, uses attended conduct and leaves the
  liveness limits unarmed. Every other automatic launch composes the recurring
  queue conduct (`prompt-queue.md`; see
  [prompt composition](../../prompt-composition/SKILL.md#session-conduct)) and arms the idle timeout:
  `COGA_REPL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` > `[launch].idle_timeout` > 900 s (`0` or non-finite
  disarms); `COGA_REPL_MAX_SESSION` / `[launch].max_session` caps wall clock.
- `--agent <type>` is an ephemeral override for every agent-backed period in the
  sweep; `ticket.py` periods keep their deterministic path.
- `--all <path>` discovers Coga workspaces below an explicit path (skipping
  dependency/tool trees, `_` trees and Coga temp-control parents), omits
  unconfigured checkouts by count, runs one checkout per remote workspace in a
  fresh process, sequentially, and exits non-zero naming failed repos. Every
  other checkout of the same remote workspace gets a `--clone-only` child,
  which runs only clone-scoped templates. Owner mismatches are skipped and
  named. Each child refreshes control before reading templates or periods;
  stale or diverged control refuses service. Off-branch children use a
  temporary control worktree without switching or stashing the operator's
  checkout.
- When catch-up fails on a behind control branch and the sole pending change
  is an unstaged, complete-line append to the existing regular log, the reason
  identifies a possible unpublished tail and offers
  [publication recovery](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#a-stranded-log-tail-blocking-catch-up).
  It preserves the tail and the refusal; no recovery runs automatically.
- `coga recurring list` is read-only: templates, firings, period state.
  `coga recurring promote` is in [templates](../templates/SKILL.md#promotion).

Every launching entry point runs from the control branch and honors the
committed `owner = "<name>"` gate: a policy gate against two operators racing,
not a lock, with no override flag. `coga recurring list` and `promote` are
ungated.

A single-repo sweep or named launch started off control relays to an existing
control worktree of the same repo. If none exists, it refuses and names the
required control checkout. Direct `coga launch recurring/<name>` does not
relay. `--force` never bypasses the control-branch gate. Repos with Git sync
disabled or confirmed to be outside Git have no managed control checkout and
are exempt; a Git inspection failure is a refusal. Optional
[control implementation](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/docs/contexts/coga-dev/internals/recurring-control/SKILL.md)
and [temporary-worktree details](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/docs/contexts/coga-dev/internals/recurring-temp-worktrees/SKILL.md)
explain the machinery.

## Admission and unfinished runs

Agent-backed periods (including `delegate:`) need stdin and stdout TTYs; a
headless sweep skips them with a warning, before creating a period or leaving a
materialized one untouched, and continues. The skipped template keeps its scan
row, `skip (agent needs a TTY)`, rather than a `## Template errors` entry; this
headless skip is not counted in `problems:`. A current period that is not
launchable (`canceled`, `blocked`, ...) is never refused: a durable checkout
would not launch it either. A `ticket.py` period runs headless and is the shape
for unattended schedulers.

On native Windows an agent run cannot measure idleness: an armed idle
timeout warns once and the session runs with its max-session limit only
([coga/launch](../../launch/SKILL.md#options-and-exits)).

A scheduled agent run must reach `done` in one launch. When an agent launch
returns unfinished — including a human/unassigned handoff or a `coga block` —
the sweep pauses it before continuing, under its own audit actor
`system:recurring`. The next bare sweep or named launch resumes each paused
period that a human did not pause, from its recorded step and blackboard, with
no `--force` and no retry cap. Pause provenance is the latest `paused` or
`created` audit line for the period:

- **Sweep pause** (actor `system:recurring`, or a legacy `human:` pause carrying
  the "Agent recurring launch exited unfinished" suffix; the legacy match is
  text-only, so a human pause whose message ends with that suffix also
  resumes) — resumed once it has
  no open `## Blockers` asks. Until then it stays parked: resuming would only
  block again. Answer with `coga unblock recurring/<name> --answer "..."`,
  which resolves the asks and leaves the period `paused` for the next sweep to
  resume with the answer on its blackboard. The blocker-reminder job keeps those
  asks visible under its
  [eligibility and deduplication contract](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/blocker-reminders/ticket.md).
  Unreadable asks leave the period paused and report a template error; they
  are never treated as an empty blocker list.
- **Watchdog pause** (actor `system:watchdog`) — resumed on every sweep, and
  still an unresolved failure: every sweep that admits the template through the
  inactivity gate shows `needs attention (watchdog timeout; resuming)`, counts
  it in `problems:`, notifies, and exits non-zero after other work, so a
  timeout that keeps recurring stays loud while it is retried. This applies
  to the bare sweep only. In a `--force` sweep, a forced recovery that
  completes clears the problem. A named `coga recurring launch <name>` resumes
  a watchdog pause without problem or notify reporting.
- **Anything else** — a human `coga mark paused` (an assist session's logs
  `agent:<name>`) or a pause whose origin is not positively identified — stays
  parked. Resume it with `coga launch recurring/<name>` or
  `coga mark active recurring/<name>`.

A resume passes the same admission as any launch: the control-branch and
`owner` gates, and the TTY gate for agent-backed periods. Headless, a sweep
pause gets the ordinary `skip (agent needs a TTY)` row; a watchdog pause shows
`needs attention (watchdog timeout; coga launch recurring/<name>)` with the
refusal and stays a problem. Keep human gates and expected blockers out of
scheduled workflows anyway: each one costs a session, a pause and a human
answer before the period can finish.

## Failures and exit code

One template's failure never cancels the rest: the sweep records it, runs every
later due template, names all failures, and exits with the first failing code.
A resume that cannot activate its frozen agent or workflow is a per-period
refusal; the sweep continues with later templates.
A template that cannot be scanned (`## Template errors`: unloadable, bad ledger
record, failed create) is named on stderr, in the Slack alert, and in
`problems:`; on its own it does not change the exit code. A sweep with any
refused or errored template never reports "No recurring tasks due".
Two exits stop immediately: **75** (retained assist state needing
reconciliation) and **≥ 128** (interrupt). Whatever stops the loop, the
stopping task and each due task "admitted as due but never launched" are named
in `problems:`.

Absence is a failure: an admitted watchdog recovery or a created period with no
launch outcome makes the sweep exit 2, except `skip (already handled on
control)`. A create sync to control that fails is non-fatal for the task — the
created period still launches — but it is named in `problems:` and exits 2. If
the created ticket then changed under that failed sync, the scan prints
`error (…)` for the template instead of any skip, and it never launches;
`--force` keeps the ordinary admission skip. A period adopted from control
stays `skip (already handled on control)` even when publishing its log line
fails; that failure is still named in `problems:`. All of this is the sweep
path. The [autofix](../autofix/SKILL.md) loop runs afterwards without changing
the exit code.

Size exception: this topic stays over the size review thresholds, as
accepted when the recurring family was consolidated. It absorbed the former
serviced-period ledger and failures leaves; splitting it again would recreate
them, so only repo inactivity stays a separate leaf.

Retention preserves every occurrence of the greatest valid period per ref and
its winning creation/pause evidence, including absent or parked templates.
It validates the full ledger first and never erases malformed older evidence
to make a bounded reader succeed. A sweep that already published treats only
removal of obsolete valid evidence as benign, after comparing full high-water
and error state at both revisions. Added records, new errors, changed maxima
or ambiguous evidence still trigger competitor-admission refusal. Target-bound
reverse reads retain their at-least semantics and error reachability.
---
name: coga/knowledge
description: The permanent authoring rule for Coga knowledge — which surface owns a fact, one owner per fact, links never load content, when to attach versus cite a topic, and the topic size review policy.
---

# Where knowledge lives

Every fact has exactly one owning file; when two copies disagree, the owner
is right. Choose the owner by what the knowledge is:

| Knowledge | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Shared facts and contracts: behavior, invariants, edge cases, product intent used across capabilities | a local topic under the configured contexts root (`<ref>/SKILL.md`), or the package owner of a shipped topic |
| Reusable process: how to do a thing | a skill (`coga/skills/<ref>/SKILL.md` or bundled) |
| One ticket-defined capability's behavior and procedure | its command ticket (`bootstrap/<name>/ticket.md`) or recurring template (`recurring/<name>/ticket.md`) |
| Maintenance procedures specific to that capability | supporting files beside its persistent ticket, linked for reading when needed |
| Per-ticket field guide: a summary carried by new tickets that links the owning topics | inline ticket template (`src/coga/resources/ticket.md`) |
| One task's temporary working state | that ticket's blackboard ([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)) |
| Execution history | `coga/log.md`, written only by CLI commands |
| Dated evidence, completed investigations, archived proposals, and other retired history | the repo's dated archive, outside the contexts root |

Humans and agents read the same owning file. Do not keep a short agent
rendition beside a longer human one: that is two owners of one fact, and the
copies drift independently. For shared facts, pick the topic whose subject
already covers the neighbouring facts; when two fit, the more narrowly
attached one wins, because the fact then costs tokens only where it is needed.

Durability alone does not make a document a context. Command tickets and
recurring templates persist; their individual executions and period tasks do
not. Keep a job's contract with the job: phone-home owns its snapshot boundary,
and Dream owns its phase order. Extract shared facts into a context and
reusable procedures into a skill when other capabilities need them.

Keep maintenance instructions separate from instructions for each run. A
template may link a sibling runbook, but recurring creation copies only
`ticket.py`, not supporting Markdown. Name the persistent template path when
directing a period to a supporting file; do not assume it is beside that
period's ticket. Skills and runbooks remain readable documentation for humans.

An owner decision *not* to act ("we looked at X and chose not to do it") is
product intent, so it belongs with X's standing owner: the shared topic, skill,
command ticket or recurring template, never only the temporary task that
recorded it. The lifecycle retires work tickets and period tasks; a decision
left in one gets re-raised. State what was declined, why, and what would reopen it.

The same retirement breaks links. Retro and `coga delete` remove a ticket
without repairing inbound references, so a topic that names a ticket by path
as the owner of an open question dangles once it retires. Point durable
surfaces at the question's standing owner, not at the transient ticket working
it, and grep for inbound references to a slug before it retires.

## Narrative links, never restates

An index, README, overview, or neighbouring topic may summarize and link to
the owner, but carries no specification-grade detail: no ordered lists, exact
names, counts or field lists that can drift on their own. "Launch stacks
conduct before task material, ticket last; the order is in
`coga/prompt-composition`" is a summary; copying the layer list is a second
specification. Command semantics live with their owning capability. A command
ticket or recurring template owns its own behavior (`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`
owns `coga retire`); rules several jobs share stay in a topic the ticket links.
`coga/cli` is an index, and installed `coga <cmd> --help` is the syntax authority.

**Sync rule.** A PR that changes an owner greps other surfaces for the fact
and fixes or deletes any restatement in the same PR. No test enforces this
across surfaces; the authoring rule is the enforcement and Dream's knowledge
scan is the backstop. A shipped definition has one committed owner, its
package copy; a repo copy of the same ref is a deliberate local override, a
separate artifact, not a second owner to keep in sync. `CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` load in every agent session, so they carry pointers plus only the
rules needed outside `coga launch`, never an owning statement.

## Links do not load content

Composition includes attached refs only
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). A markdown link
in a topic, skill, or ticket is navigation: the agent reads the target only if
it chooses to open the file, subject to that repo’s access rules. So an
overview does not bring in its children. Knowledge a step requires must be
attached explicitly by ref or named as a required read in the task or skill;
a navigation link alone does neither.

## Attach or cite

Choose from the two audiences defined in
[context layout](../context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences): user topics
under `coga/` support operating Coga in adopting repos; the local
Coga-dev set supports developing Coga itself. Select by the task's need,
then apply the attach-or-cite test below. A shipped instruction must resolve
its required knowledge from the user set; a development link is optional
navigation, never a dependency.

For a job-owned contract or supporting file, name its persistent path and the
sections to read in the task's `## Context`. Invoke a reusable skill by ref.
Do not recreate either as a context just to put it in `contexts:`.

`contexts:` is one ticket-wide list, composed whole into every launch of
every step. Decide per ticket across all planned steps:

- **Attach** when a step must have the facts without being told to look:
  its correctness depends on rules spread across the topic, or the author
  cannot predict which facts it will hit. Test: would a launched step go
  wrong if this were absent from the prompt?
- **Cite** when steps need a few identifiable facts from a topic that is
  large relative to the rest of the prompt, or when the ticket will *edit*
  that topic (it gets read first anyway).

Measure relative size at authoring time with `approx_tokens` from
`coga launch --prompt-report`, which skips the state sweep, so a trial
`contexts:` edit stays local; do not edit lifecycle frontmatter to measure,
and do not quote sizes (they go stale). No topic is
always-attach or always-cite.

A cite is one sentence in `## Context` naming the ref and path, saying it is
cited rather than attached, and naming the sections to read, followed by the
facts the step needs, cited as module plus symbol. Do not justify it by size.
The copied facts are a snapshot for that ticket, never a second owner. Citing
does not relax the sync rule: a ticket that changes behavior a cited topic
owns updates that topic and its dependent references in the same PR.

## Topic size review policy

Each topic is a directory holding `SKILL.md` with only `name` and a
one-sentence `description` stating its scope. Targets: 60 to 160 lines and
500 to 1,500 tokens (ceil(chars/4), frontmatter included); overview topics at
most 1,000 tokens. A topic over 200 lines, 10,000 bytes, or 2,500 tokens is
reviewed for a split into narrower leaves in its namespace, so tickets can
attach only the contract they need. An exception needs a recorded reason,
written in the oversized topic itself as one closing `Size exception:`
sentence saying why it stays whole. A reason kept only on a ticket
blackboard or in a PR leaves with them, and the next reader who measures the
topic cannot tell a decision from drift.
"}

def _missing_user_issue(cfg: Config) -> Issue | None:
    """Point a user-less clone at its machine-local setup without blocking reads."""
    if cfg.current_user:
        return None
    return Issue(
        kind="missing-user",
        task="(config)",
        message=(
            "no `user` set in coga.local.toml — read-only commands work, "
            "but anything that creates or moves work will fail; add "
            '`user = "<name>"` (the file is gitignored, so every clone '
            "sets its own)"
        ),
        severity="warn",
    )


def run(
    cfg: Config,
    idle_hours: float = 72.0,
    max_blackboard_bytes: int = BLACKBOARD_WARN_BYTES,
    check_slack: bool = False,
    check_github: bool = False,
    fix: bool = False,
) -> Report:
    report = Report(generated_at=_now_iso())

    # `coga validate` loads config with `require_user=False` so a teammate's
    # fresh clone (no gitignored `coga.local.toml` yet) can run diagnostics at
    # all — so the missing name must surface here as a finding instead of
    # silently validating clean.
    missing_user = _missing_user_issue(cfg)
    if missing_user is not None:
        report.issues.append(missing_user)
    important_webhook = _important_webhook_issue(cfg)
    if important_webhook is not None:
        report.issues.append(important_webhook)

    try:
        refs = list_tasks(cfg)
    except DuplicateTaskSlugError as exc:
        report.issues.append(_duplicate_slug_issue(exc))
        return report

    if fix:
        report.fixes.extend(apply_safe_fixes(cfg, only=refs))

    if check_slack:
        report.issues.extend(_notification_issues(cfg))

    if check_github:
        report.issues.extend(_github_issues(cfg))

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    for ref in refs:
        report.issues.extend(
            _check_one_task(
                cfg,
                ref,
                max_blackboard_bytes=max_blackboard_bytes,
                idle_hours=idle_hours,
                now=now,
            )
        )

    report.issues.extend(_check_task_numbering(refs))
    report.issues.extend(_check_recurring_templates(cfg))
    report.issues.extend(_check_shebang_executables(cfg))
    report.issues.extend(_check_repo_resources(cfg))

    report.ok_count = _ok_count(refs, report.issues)
    return report


def validate_task(
    cfg: Config,
    slug: str,
    *,
    fix: bool = False,
    max_blackboard_bytes: int = BLACKBOARD_WARN_BYTES,
    idle_hours: float = 72.0,
) -> Report:
    """Validate exactly one task directory. Used by `coga validate --task`
    and by every Coga-owned command that mutates a task file."""
    report = Report(generated_at=_now_iso())
    missing_user = _missing_user_issue(cfg)
    if missing_user is not None:
        report.issues.append(missing_user)
    important_webhook = _important_webhook_issue(cfg)
    if important_webhook is not None:
        report.issues.append(important_webhook)
    try:
        ref = resolve_task(cfg, slug)
    except DuplicateTaskSlugError as exc:
        report.issues.append(_duplicate_slug_issue(exc))
        return report
    except TaskNotFoundError as exc:
        report.issues.append(Issue(
            kind="unknown-task",
            task=slug,
            message=str(exc),
            severity="error",
        ))
        return report

    if fix:
        report.fixes.extend(apply_safe_fixes(cfg, only=[ref]))

    report.issues.extend(
        _check_one_task(
            cfg,
            ref,
            max_blackboard_bytes=max_blackboard_bytes,
            idle_hours=idle_hours,
            now=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )
    )
    report.ok_count = _ok_count([ref], report.issues)
    return report


def _main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Coga repo validator")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit JSON instead of text.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--task",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Validate exactly one task slug.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--fix",
        action="store_true",
        help="Apply conservative safe repairs before reporting.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--idle-hours", type=float, default=72.0)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-blackboard-kb",
        type=float,
        default=BLACKBOARD_WARN_BYTES / 1024,
        help="Blackboard size above which to warn about prompt bloat.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--check-slack",
        action="store_true",
        help="Also probe the Slack webhook with an empty-text payload (network call).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--check-github",
        action="store_true",
        help="Also probe git/GitHub auth readiness via git/gh (network call).",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        cfg = load_config(require_user=False)
    except ConfigError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"{exc}\n")
        return 2

    if args.task is not None:
        if args.check_slack:
            sys.stderr.write("--check-slack is not supported with --task\n")
            return 2
        if args.check_github:
            sys.stderr.write("--check-github is not supported with --task\n")
            return 2
        report = validate_task(
            cfg,
            args.task,
            fix=args.fix,
            max_blackboard_bytes=int(args.max_blackboard_kb * 1024),
            idle_hours=args.idle_hours,
        )
    else:
        report = run(
            cfg,
            idle_hours=args.idle_hours,
            max_blackboard_bytes=int(args.max_blackboard_kb * 1024),
            check_slack=args.check_slack,
            check_github=args.check_github,
            fix=args.fix,
        )

    if args.json:
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "generated_at": report.generated_at,
            "ok_count": report.ok_count,
            "fixes": [asdict(f) for f in report.fixes],
            "issues": [asdict(i) for i in report.issues],
        }
        json.dump(payload, sys.stdout, indent=2)
        sys.stdout.write("\n")
    else:
        if not report.issues:
            for fix_item in report.fixes:
                print(f"[FIX] {fix_item.task}: {fix_item.kind} — {fix_item.message}")
            print(f"All good ({report.ok_count} tasks checked).")
        else:
            for fix_item in report.fixes:
                print(f"[FIX] {fix_item.task}: {fix_item.kind} — {fix_item.message}")
            for issue in report.issues:
                sev = issue.severity.upper()
                print(f"[{sev}] {issue.task}: {issue.kind} — {issue.message}")

    # Exit code: 0 if no errors, 1 if errors, 2 on tool failure.
    return 1 if any(i.severity == "error" for i in report.issues) else 0

def test_windows_cli_uses_utf8_when_output_is_redirected(clone, monkeypatch):
    import io
    import sys
    from types import SimpleNamespace
    from coga import cli

    def command():
        print("Café → 語")
        print("Café → 語", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(0)

    output, errors = io.BytesIO(), io.BytesIO()
    stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(output, encoding="cp1252")
    stderr = io.TextIOWrapper(errors, encoding="cp1252")
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "os", SimpleNamespace(name="nt"))
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "app", command)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "stdout", stdout)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "stderr", stderr)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["coga", "--help"])
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        main()
    assert exc.value.code == 0
    stdout.flush()
    stderr.flush()
    assert output.getvalue().decode("utf-8").strip() == "Café → 語"
    assert errors.getvalue().decode("utf-8").strip() == "Café → 語"

@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure", [SystemExit(9), OSError("spawn failed"), KeyboardInterrupt()])
def test_control_relay_suppresses_parent_sweep_and_resets_after_failure(
    clone: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, failure: BaseException
) -> None:
    from coga.recurring_runner import control_relay_started

    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.argv", ["coga", "recurring"])
    sweeps: list[object] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr("coga.git.sync_coga_state", sweeps.append)
    prior = control_relay_started.get()

    def relay() -> None:
        control_relay_started.set(True)
        raise failure

def _missing_user_issue(cfg: Config) -> Issue | None:
    """Point a user-less clone at its machine-local setup without blocking reads."""
    if cfg.current_user:
        return None
    return Issue(
        kind="missing-user",
        task="(config)",
        message=(
            "no `user` set in coga.local.toml — read-only commands work, "
            "but anything that creates or moves work will fail; add "
            '`user = "<name>"` (the file is gitignored, so every clone '
            "sets its own)"
        ),
        severity="warn",
    )


def run(
    cfg: Config,
    idle_hours: float = 72.0,
    max_blackboard_bytes: int = BLACKBOARD_WARN_BYTES,
    check_slack: bool = False,
    check_github: bool = False,
    fix: bool = False,
) -> Report:
    report = Report(generated_at=_now_iso())

    # `coga validate` loads config with `require_user=False` so a teammate's
    # fresh clone (no gitignored `coga.local.toml` yet) can run diagnostics at
    # all — so the missing name must surface here as a finding instead of
    # silently validating clean.
    missing_user = _missing_user_issue(cfg)
    if missing_user is not None:
        report.issues.append(missing_user)
    important_webhook = _important_webhook_issue(cfg)
    if important_webhook is not None:
        report.issues.append(important_webhook)

    try:
        refs = list_tasks(cfg)
    except DuplicateTaskSlugError as exc:
        report.issues.append(_duplicate_slug_issue(exc))
        return report

    if fix:
        report.fixes.extend(apply_safe_fixes(cfg, only=refs))

    if check_slack:
        report.issues.extend(_notification_issues(cfg))

    if check_github:
        report.issues.extend(_github_issues(cfg))

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    for ref in refs:
        report.issues.extend(
            _check_one_task(
                cfg,
                ref,
                max_blackboard_bytes=max_blackboard_bytes,
                idle_hours=idle_hours,
                now=now,
            )
        )

    report.issues.extend(_check_task_numbering(refs))
    report.issues.extend(_check_recurring_templates(cfg))
    report.issues.extend(_check_shebang_executables(cfg))
    report.issues.extend(_check_repo_resources(cfg))

    report.ok_count = _ok_count(refs, report.issues)
    return report


def validate_task(
    cfg: Config,
    slug: str,
    *,
    fix: bool = False,
    max_blackboard_bytes: int = BLACKBOARD_WARN_BYTES,
    idle_hours: float = 72.0,
) -> Report:
    """Validate exactly one task directory. Used by `coga validate --task`
    and by every Coga-owned command that mutates a task file."""
    report = Report(generated_at=_now_iso())
    missing_user = _missing_user_issue(cfg)
    if missing_user is not None:
        report.issues.append(missing_user)
    important_webhook = _important_webhook_issue(cfg)
    if important_webhook is not None:
        report.issues.append(important_webhook)
    try:
        ref = resolve_task(cfg, slug)
    except DuplicateTaskSlugError as exc:
        report.issues.append(_duplicate_slug_issue(exc))
        return report
    except TaskNotFoundError as exc:
        report.issues.append(Issue(
            kind="unknown-task",
            task=slug,
            message=str(exc),
            severity="error",
        ))
        return report

    if fix:
        report.fixes.extend(apply_safe_fixes(cfg, only=[ref]))

    report.issues.extend(
        _check_one_task(
            cfg,
            ref,
            max_blackboard_bytes=max_blackboard_bytes,
            idle_hours=idle_hours,
            now=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )
    )
    report.ok_count = _ok_count([ref], report.issues)
    return report


def _main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Coga repo validator")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit JSON instead of text.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--task",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Validate exactly one task slug.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--fix",
        action="store_true",
        help="Apply conservative safe repairs before reporting.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--idle-hours", type=float, default=72.0)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-blackboard-kb",
        type=float,
        default=BLACKBOARD_WARN_BYTES / 1024,
        help="Blackboard size above which to warn about prompt bloat.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--check-slack",
        action="store_true",
        help="Also probe the Slack webhook with an empty-text payload (network call).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--check-github",
        action="store_true",
        help="Also probe git/GitHub auth readiness via git/gh (network call).",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        cfg = load_config(require_user=False)
    except ConfigError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"{exc}\n")
        return 2

    if args.task is not None:
        if args.check_slack:
            sys.stderr.write("--check-slack is not supported with --task\n")
            return 2
        if args.check_github:
            sys.stderr.write("--check-github is not supported with --task\n")
            return 2
        report = validate_task(
            cfg,
            args.task,
            fix=args.fix,
            max_blackboard_bytes=int(args.max_blackboard_kb * 1024),
            idle_hours=args.idle_hours,
        )
    else:
        report = run(
            cfg,
            idle_hours=args.idle_hours,
            max_blackboard_bytes=int(args.max_blackboard_kb * 1024),
            check_slack=args.check_slack,
            check_github=args.check_github,
            fix=args.fix,
        )

    if args.json:
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "generated_at": report.generated_at,
            "ok_count": report.ok_count,
            "fixes": [asdict(f) for f in report.fixes],
            "issues": [asdict(i) for i in report.issues],
        }
        json.dump(payload, sys.stdout, indent=2)
        sys.stdout.write("\n")
    else:
        if not report.issues:
            for fix_item in report.fixes:
                print(f"[FIX] {fix_item.task}: {fix_item.kind} — {fix_item.message}")
            print(f"All good ({report.ok_count} tasks checked).")
        else:
            for fix_item in report.fixes:
                print(f"[FIX] {fix_item.task}: {fix_item.kind} — {fix_item.message}")
            for issue in report.issues:
                sev = issue.severity.upper()
                print(f"[{sev}] {issue.task}: {issue.kind} — {issue.message}")

    # Exit code: 0 if no errors, 1 if errors, 2 on tool failure.
    return 1 if any(i.severity == "error" for i in report.issues) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(_main())

name: coga/configuration
description: The shared `coga.toml` versus machine-local `coga.local.toml` split, each file's key allowlist, fail-loud unknown-key and migration errors, and where `env:` indirection works.

# Configuration

Coga reads two files from the Coga root:

- **`coga.toml`**, committed: repo policy every clone must agree on.
- **`coga.local.toml`**, gitignored: facts about this machine and operator.
  `COGA_LOCAL_CONFIG` can point a process at an absolute path instead, so a
  Coga process in another checkout of the same repo, such as a relay
  worktree, reads the operator's local settings.

Both are validated against fixed schemas on every command that loads config.
Two invocations read neither file, so neither validates config nor sweeps
state: `coga --version`, and `--help`/`-h` under a built-in command (for
example `coga launch --help`). Top-level `coga --help`
still loads config to list the repo's `[aliases]`. Never commit real
credentials. Use indirection ([coga/secrets](../secrets/SKILL.md)).

## Choosing an agent

Init declares the agents whose CLI it found on `PATH` and comments out the
`[agents.*]` table of every other supported agent. So with one agent installed
you need no config edit: that agent is the only declared type and therefore the
default. To add another, install its CLI and uncomment its table in
`coga/coga.toml`.

In a repo that declares both, choose which one new tasks get with this
top-level setting, placed before any `[table]` in `coga/coga.local.toml`:

```toml
default_agent = "codex"
```

This does not change an already activated ticket or select the interviewer
for `coga chat` and `coga ticket`. Use `coga chat --agent codex` or
`coga ticket "Your task title" --agent codex` for those sessions.

One limit to know in a repo that declares Codex but not Claude Code. The
packaged `coga chat` and `coga ticket` tickets pin `agent: claude`, and a
`--agent` override cannot repair a pin that names an undeclared type, so
`coga chat` fails there even with `--agent codex`; `coga ticket --agent codex`
works, because authoring checks the override first. `coga build` works, because
init points its ticket at the agent it found. Uncommenting `[agents.claude]`
gets `coga chat` past that routing check, since the pin is a name matched
against this file — but the session then needs the `claude` binary like any
other launch. Making those commands agent-agnostic is the real fix and is
tracked separately.

The comments beside `default_agent` and `[agents.*]` in the
[shipped configuration](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/coga.toml)
own precedence and routing details. Workflow roles and peer selection are
explained in [coga/workflows](../workflows/SKILL.md); the
[first-task walk](../first-task/SKILL.md) covers the prerequisites for a PR
with either one agent or a peer reviewer.

## Allowlists

`coga.toml` top level: `version` (must be `1`), `default_status`,
`default_agent`, `owner`, `agents`, `notification`, `git`, `launch`, `ticket`, `aliases`,
`extensions`, `layout`, `autofix`, `telemetry`, `recurring`, `log`.

`coga.local.toml` top level: `user`, `default_agent`, `agents`,
`notification`, `git`, `upstream`, `telemetry`, `authoring`.

`default_agent` is a string in both files. The local value wins, and each
present value must name a type in the merged `[agents.*]`; it is validated at
load. Precedence, freezing at activation, and what it does not move are
explained beside the key in the shipped `coga.toml`.

# Packaging Coga's resources

## Where bundled resources live

Bundled skills, contexts, reusable workflows, and command tickets are authored
under `src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/`. Runtime resolvers
(`paths.resolve_context_path`, `resolve_skill_path`, `resolve_workflow_path`,
`tasks.resolve_bootstrap`) check the repo first and then read the package; no
`coga/bootstrap/` mirror is materialized. Optional domain skills are not
packaged; operators install them with `coga skill install`
([coga/skill-management](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/skill-management/SKILL.md)).

**Local-first also applies to this repo.** A live `coga/<kind>/<name>`
shadows the packaged copy; where none exists, the packaged file is what this
repo resolves and freezes. This repo has no live `coga/workflows/code/`, so
editing `bootstrap/workflows/code/*.md` changes what `mark_active` freezes into
Coga's own tickets. Check which side is live before assuming an edit is
downstream-only.

## Distribution states for a context

- **Bootstrap fallback**: `templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/<ref>/SKILL.md`
  (every `coga/*` topic). `coga init` skips `bootstrap/`;
  `paths.resolve_context_path` reads the package copy
  (`bootstrap_context_path`) when the repo has no local `<ref>/SKILL.md`.
- **Init-seeded**: `templates/coga/contexts/**`, today only the scaffolds
  `.gitignore` and `_template/SKILL.md`. `commands/update.py`
  `copy_fresh_templates` copies only the reviewed `FRESH_SCAFFOLDS`
  allowlist once; nothing reads the packaged original at runtime.
- **Local-only**: no packaged copy, resolved first and unknown to other repos
  (a repo's `product/` topics, or this repo's `coga-dev/` set).

Resolution is local, then `bootstrap/contexts/`, then `None`, which `compose`
turns into a `ComposeError`. Skills and workflows have the same split:
fallback only from `bootstrap/{skills,workflows}/`. Every reusable workflow
and skill, including `direct/body`, `build/onboarding` and the recurring
workflows, is now a bootstrap battery; `templates/coga/{skills,workflows}/`
hold only the ignored `_template` starters. A present but unusable local
override (`paths.local_definition_entry`) raises `LocalOverrideError` rather
than selecting the packaged copy.

**Bundled launchers may only name fallback contexts.** A bundled
`bootstrap/<verb>/ticket.md`, or a bundled skill that tells the agent to apply
a context, must name contexts that resolve from `bootstrap/contexts/`, because
an init-seeded copy may be pruned or predate the repo.
`tests/test_packaging.py::test_bundled_bootstrap_tickets_attach_only_bootstrap_contexts`
enforces this.

## Package ownership and repo state

The audience criterion belongs to
[context layout](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences):
user topics operate shipped surfaces; Coga-dev topics explain developing Coga.
The complete `coga-dev/` namespace, including attachments, stays local. A
shipped surface may not require it; optional development navigation uses an
absolute GitHub link.

Every shipped definition has one committed owner under `src/coga/resources/`.
This repo has completed its cutover: user topics live only in package
`bootstrap/contexts/`, reusable skills/workflows in `bootstrap/{skills,workflows}/`,

description: The writer's contract for a ticket blackboard — locating the fence, scoping edits, live sections and superseded designs, the draft-activation readiness check, size limits and their remedy, and safe concurrent writes. Attach to tickets whose work writes blackboards programmatically.

# Writing to a ticket blackboard

The blackboard is everything below the `<!-- coga:blackboard -->` fence in a
ticket: working memory shared by human and agent and carried between
stateless sessions. Its live state is composed into every launch
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)); `coga/log.md`,
written only by CLI commands, holds lifecycle history and is never composed.
Working state the next run must read goes here and stays small; history goes
in the log.

## The fence

The fence counts only as a whole line: no leading indentation, optional
trailing whitespace. Markdown is not parsed, so an own-line fence inside a
code block counts, while an inline mention does not.

- **Never locate the fence by substring** (`split`, `find`, `partition`,
  unanchored `grep`/`sed`): a quoted fence in prose truncates the body.
- **Exactly one fence.** Readers fail on zero or several. Bootstrap command
  tickets legitimately have none.
- **Scope each edit.** Compute every transform on the blackboard region, never
  on whole-file text, so a `## Heading` pattern cannot hit the body, and never
  reformat the YAML while writing below the fence.

What may be edited above the fence is owned by
[coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md) (agents: `contexts` and body sections).

## Section regimes

Match the section's regime; do not invent a fourth.

- **Live state: rewrite in place.** One current value per named line. `## Dev`
  (`branch:`, `worktree:`, `pr:`) is canonical; its shape is in
  the ticket template's guide comment. Old values live in git.
- **Record: append, never delete.** `## Superseded designs` takes dated
  entries (shape [below](#superseded-designs);
  only an archive pointer composes). `## Blockers` takes one checkbox per ask;
  `coga unblock` marks it `- [x]` and appends `resolved:`. Blocker readers
  ignore fenced examples and superseded sections.
  The writer does not (known limitation, unfixed): when a real ask is open,
  `coga unblock` (`blackboard.resolve_open_blockers`) also flips `- [ ]`
  examples in fences and superseded sections and appends `resolved:` to
  them, so keep example blockers out of a blackboard that may be unblocked.
- **Authoring scratch: synthesize before launch.** `## Evaluator review`,
  `## Ticket authoring notes`, `## Proposals`. The `bootstrap/ticket` cleanup
  folds durable substance into the body; for a draft it keeps
  `## Superseded designs` and resets the rest to the stock placeholder; for a
  non-draft it removes only the authoring sections it used.

## Superseded designs

When a design changes, rewrite `## Description` and `## Context` to describe
current work, with live requirements under `###` subheadings. Other top-level
body sections do not compose. Move the abandoned plan below the blackboard
fence into one `## Superseded designs` section; append dated entries oldest
to newest:

```markdown
## Superseded designs

### YYYY-MM-DD — <abandoned direction>

Superseded by: <current direction or decision>
Reason: <why the ticket pivoted>

<prior plan, acceptance details, and evidence worth retaining>
```

Retain enough to understand or reconsider the old plan, with copied headings
at `####` or deeper inside each entry. Keep history in this single section,

**Local-first also applies to this repo.** A live `coga/<kind>/<name>`
shadows the packaged copy; where none exists, the packaged file is what this
repo resolves and freezes. This repo has no live `coga/workflows/code/`, so
editing `bootstrap/workflows/code/*.md` changes what `mark_active` freezes into
Coga's own tickets. Check which side is live before assuming an edit is
downstream-only.

## Distribution states for a context

- **Bootstrap fallback**: `templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/<ref>/SKILL.md`
  (every `coga/*` topic). `coga init` skips `bootstrap/`;
  `paths.resolve_context_path` reads the package copy
  (`bootstrap_context_path`) when the repo has no local `<ref>/SKILL.md`.
- **Init-seeded**: `templates/coga/contexts/**`, today only the scaffolds
  `.gitignore` and `_template/SKILL.md`. `commands/update.py`
  `copy_fresh_templates` copies only the reviewed `FRESH_SCAFFOLDS`
  allowlist once; nothing reads the packaged original at runtime.
- **Local-only**: no packaged copy, resolved first and unknown to other repos
  (a repo's `product/` topics, or this repo's `coga-dev/` set).

Resolution is local, then `bootstrap/contexts/`, then `None`, which `compose`
turns into a `ComposeError`. Skills and workflows have the same split:
fallback only from `bootstrap/{skills,workflows}/`. Every reusable workflow
and skill, including `direct/body`, `build/onboarding` and the recurring
workflows, is now a bootstrap battery; `templates/coga/{skills,workflows}/`
hold only the ignored `_template` starters. A present but unusable local
override (`paths.local_definition_entry`) raises `LocalOverrideError` rather
than selecting the packaged copy.

**Bundled launchers may only name fallback contexts.** A bundled
`bootstrap/<verb>/ticket.md`, or a bundled skill that tells the agent to apply
a context, must name contexts that resolve from `bootstrap/contexts/`, because
an init-seeded copy may be pruned or predate the repo.
`tests/test_packaging.py::test_bundled_bootstrap_tickets_attach_only_bootstrap_contexts`
enforces this.

## Package ownership and repo state

The audience criterion belongs to
[context layout](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences):
user topics operate shipped surfaces; Coga-dev topics explain developing Coga.
The complete `coga-dev/` namespace, including attachments, stays local. A
shipped surface may not require it; optional development navigation uses an
absolute GitHub link.

Every shipped definition has one committed owner under `src/coga/resources/`.
This repo has completed its cutover: user topics live only in package

name: coga/blackboard
description: The writer's contract for a ticket blackboard — locating the fence, scoping edits, live sections and superseded designs, the draft-activation readiness check, size limits and their remedy, and safe concurrent writes. Attach to tickets whose work writes blackboards programmatically.
---

# Writing to a ticket blackboard

The blackboard is everything below the `<!-- coga:blackboard -->` fence in a
ticket: working memory shared by human and agent and carried between
stateless sessions. Its live state is composed into every launch
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)); `coga/log.md`,
written only by CLI commands, holds lifecycle history and is never composed.
Working state the next run must read goes here and stays small; history goes
in the log.

## The fence

The fence counts only as a whole line: no leading indentation, optional
trailing whitespace. Markdown is not parsed, so an own-line fence inside a
code block counts, while an inline mention does not.

- **Never locate the fence by substring** (`split`, `find`, `partition`,
  unanchored `grep`/`sed`): a quoted fence in prose truncates the body.
- **Exactly one fence.** Readers fail on zero or several. Bootstrap command
  tickets legitimately have none.
- **Scope each edit.** Compute every transform on the blackboard region, never
  on whole-file text, so a `## Heading` pattern cannot hit the body, and never
  reformat the YAML while writing below the fence.

What may be edited above the fence is owned by
[coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md) (agents: `contexts` and body sections).

## Section regimes

Match the section's regime; do not invent a fourth.

- **Live state: rewrite in place.** One current value per named line. `## Dev`
  (`branch:`, `worktree:`, `pr:`) is canonical; its shape is in
  the ticket template's guide comment. Old values live in git.
- **Record: append, never delete.** `## Superseded designs` takes dated
  entries (shape [below](#superseded-designs);
  only an archive pointer composes). `## Blockers` takes one checkbox per ask;
  `coga unblock` marks it `- [x]` and appends `resolved:`. Blocker readers
  ignore fenced examples and superseded sections.
  The writer does not (known limitation, unfixed): when a real ask is open,
  `coga unblock` (`blackboard.resolve_open_blockers`) also flips `- [ ]`
  examples in fences and superseded sections and appends `resolved:` to
  them, so keep example blockers out of a blackboard that may be unblocked.
- **Authoring scratch: synthesize before launch.** `## Evaluator review`,
  `## Ticket authoring notes`, `## Proposals`. The `bootstrap/ticket` cleanup
  folds durable substance into the body; for a draft it keeps
  `## Superseded designs` and resets the rest to the stock placeholder; for a
  non-draft it removes only the authoring sections it used.

## Superseded designs

When a design changes, rewrite `## Description` and `## Context` to describe
current work, with live requirements under `###` subheadings. Other top-level
body sections do not compose. Move the abandoned plan below the blackboard
fence into one `## Superseded designs` section; append dated entries oldest
to newest:

```markdown
## Superseded designs

### YYYY-MM-DD — <abandoned direction>

Superseded by: <current direction or decision>
Reason: <why the ticket pivoted>

<prior plan, acceptance details, and evidence worth retaining>
```

Retain enough to understand or reconsider the old plan, with copied headings
at `####` or deeper inside each entry. Keep history in this single section,

This walk assumes Coga is installed ([Get started](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/README.md#get-started)) and
the repo is initialized with your name set ([coga/init](../init/SKILL.md)).
Each step links to the topic that owns its contract.

## 0. Check readiness

Use a macOS, Linux or native Windows terminal; Windows needs the
README's [native Windows notes](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/README.md#get-started).
For this walk's GitHub PR, start on clean, current `main` (or your configured
control branch) in a repo with a remote you can push to. Install GitHub CLI
and run `gh auth login`; Git push credentials must also work.

The example uses `code/with-review`. With the default configuration it needs
both Claude Code and Codex installed and authenticated, because the second
agent reviews the first agent's work. If you use only one agent, choose
`code/with-self-review` in the create command below. It keeps the final human
PR gate but uses the same agent for implementation and self-review
([coga/workflows](../workflows/SKILL.md)). Keep the human gate for a first
task; `code/agent-merge`, where the agents merge the reviewed PR themselves,
is for later work once you trust the loop.

```sh
coga validate            # repo and task structure; non-zero exit on errors
coga validate --json     # the same, machine-readable
coga status              # the task triage view
```

A repo-wide `coga validate` also requires every file that starts with a `#!`
line under the skills root or the packaged bootstrap skills to be executable;
a shebang declares the file is run directly, so a missing executable bit is a
`non-executable-script` error. `coga validate --task <slug>` does not run this
check. Fix your own file with `chmod +x <file>` and commit the new mode, or
use `git add --chmod=+x <file>` where Git ignores filesystem modes. A hit
under the packaged `bootstrap/skills` comes from the installed Coga, not your
repo: upgrade or reinstall Coga (`uv tool upgrade coga` for the recommended
uv install). On POSIX the
check reads the working-tree mode; on Windows, or with a repo-local
`core.fileMode=false`, it reads the git index and skips untracked files. It
skips a root that has neither source.

Run `coga validate` again after any config, workflow, or ticket change. It
warns when `user` is unset. Network probes are opt-in:
`coga validate --check-github` checks git and `gh` auth readiness, and
`--check-slack` checks the Slack webhook
([coga/notifications](../notifications/SKILL.md)). Neither combines with
`--task`.

These checks do not test agent authentication or complete a first task.

On an empty repo, `init` seeded an onboarding ticket. `coga build` is a
default alias for `launch coga-build`: one question, an agent-led chat, a
short vision, then a batch of starter tickets, offered for launch only once
the vision and the batch are confirmed on the control branch. Use `coga build --agent
codex` for Codex. It dispatches through `coga launch`, so it needs an
initialized repo. Coga never installs an agent CLI: when the configured one
cannot be found, the launch fails and names the `[agents.*]` table to fix in
`coga.toml` ([coga/init](../init/SKILL.md)). There is no separate `coga setup`.

## 1. Create a draft

A ticket is one unit of work: a markdown file under `coga/tasks/`
([coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md)). Either scaffold one:

```sh
coga create "Add a health-check endpoint" --workflow code/with-review
```

then fill in `## Description` and `## Context`, or let an agent interview
you into one with `coga ticket "Add a health-check endpoint"`. To plan a
batch, talk it through in `coga chat` and let the session create the drafts.
Drafts are cheap and need no workflow yet, but a ticket cannot be activated
without one ([coga/workflows](../workflows/SKILL.md)).

For a Codex interview, use
`coga ticket "Add a health-check endpoint" --agent codex` or
`coga chat --agent codex`. The interviewer's selection is separate from the
task's main agent. New tasks use the configured default at activation; see
[agent configuration](../configuration/SKILL.md#choosing-an-agent).

## 2. Launch it

```sh
coga launch add-a-health-check-endpoint --prompt-report   # inspect, don't launch
coga launch add-a-health-check-endpoint
```

`--prompt-report` shows the composed layers and their token counts
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). Typing
`coga launch` approves a draft or paused ticket; a launch refused by a
preflight leaves the ticket unchanged ([coga/launch](../launch/SKILL.md)).

The session is attended: you watch and talk to the agent. It does the step's
work, records findings on the blackboard using its inline
guidance, and finishes with `coga bump`.
For a multi-step workflow such as `code/with-review`, the supervisor then
starts the next agent step, rotating to the peer agent for review
([coga/workflows](../workflows/SKILL.md)).

## 3. Review and merge

The final `review` step is a human gate with an open PR. Review and merge it
on GitHub, then run `coga bump <task>`; bumping the final step marks the
ticket `done`. Confirm `coga show <task>` reports `done` and inspect the
merged result; a successful install, prompt report, or agent exit alone
does not establish a completed task. A repo that schedules the
`autoclose-merged` recurring sweep
also closes merged tickets on its next run, but that is opt-in
([coga/recurring](../recurring/SKILL.md)). To decline the work instead, use
`coga mark canceled <task> --message "<reason>"`, which stays distinct from
completed work. States and gates: [coga/lifecycle](../lifecycle/SKILL.md).

`coga show <task>` prints the whole ticket, history included.

## What you touched

- **Ticket**: the durable unit of work, in files rather than a session.
- **Workflow**: ordered steps, frozen into the ticket when it activates.
- **Blackboard**: scratch memory that survives torn-down sessions.
- **Composition**: each prompt is rebuilt from files on disk at launch.
- **Correction loop**: when an agent is misled, fix and commit the context
  or workflow that misled it; the next launch composes the fix
  ([coga/architecture](../architecture/SKILL.md)).

# Coga codebase

The repo separates implementation from the OS it operates:

- **`src/coga/`**: the kernel package and CLI.
- **`src/coga_edge/`**: edge job implementations shipped in the same wheel;
  placement is owned by [coga-dev/microkernel](../microkernel/SKILL.md).
- **`coga/`** plus the configured contexts root (`docs/contexts/` in this
  repo): the Coga OS this repo operates on. Layout is owned by
  [coga/context-layout](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/context-layout/SKILL.md).

## Source map

- `src/coga_edge/phone_home.py`: the default telemetry implementation behind
  the repo shim; [phone-home ticket](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/phone-home/ticket.md) owns its contract.

- `src/coga/commands/`: one Typer entrypoint per command. Thin entrypoints
  with no business logic are the target; `init.py` still carries substantial
  logic. Launch's command adapter calls shared `coga.launch`. `update.py` (init's
  template-copy helpers) and `common.py` are shared helpers, not commands.
- `config.py` (shared/local TOML, fixed schema; ticket secret refs in
  `parse_inline_secrets`, `select_launch_secrets`, `build_launch_env`,
  `scrub_op_auth_env`), `compose.py` (prompt layers),
  `tasks.py` / `taskfile.py` / `blackboard.py` (ticket IO),
  `workflow.py` / `bump.py` / `step_gate.py` / `mark.py` (steps, gates,
  status), `validate.py` (`coga validate`).
  `config.load_config` rejects unknown keys through `_reject_unknown_keys`,
  `_reject_unknown_sections` and the per-table parsers; removed or misplaced
  keys get tailored errors first. Adding a config key means adding it to its
  table's allowlist and the [coga/configuration](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/configuration/SKILL.md)
  table in the same change. Only `_resolve_secret_value` runs `env:`
  indirection, for the two Slack webhook keys.
- `git.py`: the whole Git sync layer (`publish`, `refresh`,
  `prepare_control_checkout`, `state_lock`, public plumbing). Contract in [coga/state-publication](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/state-publication/SKILL.md).
- `review_conflict.py`: the human-review PR a lifecycle command opens for an
  unrankable ticket status conflict, and its merged/closed/open return path;
  shared by lifecycle commands through `commands/common.reconcile_lifecycle_ticket`
  (`coga-dev/internals/git-regressions`).
- `runner.py`: the fixed `coga run` registry; recipes live in focused modules
  (`open_pr.py`, `delete_task.py`, `autoclose.py`, `branchsweep.py`, ...).
- `oscompat.py`: per-user lock paths and descriptor locks for publication
  and chat, and owned process trees for both recurring runners and the
  Windows agent supervisor. POSIX uses flock/process groups; Windows uses
  byte-range locks and Job Objects. Its interactive mode runs
  `_nt_session_wrapper.py`, a stdlib-only script run by path under the base
  interpreter.
- `launch.py` (launch API, preparation and supervision),
  `checkout_policy.py` (pure entry-checkout selection: the frozen step's
  `checkout:`, else the legacy table for older snapshots) and
  `checkouts.py` (shared branch preparation for launch and the
  `prepare-checkout` chat recipe; [coga/checkouts](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/checkouts/SKILL.md)),
  `launch_script.py` (reserved `ticket.py` phase), `task_env.py`
  (`COGA_TASK_*`), `repl_supervisor.py` with its native Windows backend
  and command planner `repl_supervisor_nt.py` (imported only on Windows by
  the shared entry), `megalaunch.py` plus
  `service_order.py` (drain), `recurring_runner.py`, `recurring_autofix.py`,
  `recurring_clone.py`. `recurring.py` also owns the effective recurring
  catalog (`iter_template_sources`, `resolve_template_source`, `jobs.toml`
  selection); `recurring_state.py` classifies parent directories and owns
  state-only carriers (`parent_state_path`, `ensure_parent_state`), so
  definition lookup and repo-local state writes stay separate. Definition
  resolution for other refs (`resolve_skill_path`, `local_definition_entry`)
  is in `paths.py`.
- `branchcleanup.py` (per-checkout proofs), `checkout_disposal.py` (claim and
  disposal order), `retire_worklist.py` (`retires.md`).
- `dependencies.py` (supporting-tool install manifest, supported agent CLI
  scan order, and the shared missing-agent requirement).
- `skill_manager.py` (`coga skill`; `gh_skill_repo` decides GitHub-backed
  membership, `classify_gh_update_output` maps `gh` output to outcomes; a
  legacy digest that includes machine-local directories may still prove a
  tree unchanged, and status reuses update's comparisons without writing),
  `notification/`,
  `text.py` (shared ANSI stripper), `reminders.py` (sweep harness for
  downstream scripts).
- `resources/`: prompt resources and the packaged Coga OS under
  `resources/templates/coga/`; see [coga-dev/packaging](../packaging/SKILL.md).
- `tests/` (`tests/test_*.py`, named after the command or module) and
  `tests/fixtures/seeded-repo/coga/`, the seeded end-to-end fixture.

Module-level seams a new caller must respect (operator resolution, the
`prepare_active` / `mark_active` split, blackboard writers, create guards) are
in [coga-dev/codebase/gotchas](gotchas/SKILL.md).

## Contribution rules

- **Microkernel.** Core holds only shared infra with two or more real
  consumers or a reviewed co-versioned command contract. The rule and its
  exceptions are owned by [coga-dev/microkernel](../microkernel/SKILL.md).
- **Style.** Python 3.11+, 4-space indentation,
  `from __future__ import annotations`, explicit type hints, `snake_case`
  modules and functions, `PascalCase` dataclasses and exceptions, standard
  library first, small command handlers. Keep projects, skills, contexts,
  workflows, and tasks distinct.
- **Fixtures.** Changes to prompt composition, workflow freezing, config
  loading, or task creation update `tests/fixtures/seeded-repo/` or related fixtures.
